items.followUp: How does light intensity affect the rate of photosynthesis?

rubric.why: Identifies the effect of increasing carbon dioxide concentration on the rate of photosynthesis.
rubric.description: Increasing carbon dioxide concentration increases the rate of photosynthesis, provided other factors are not limiting.
rubric.how: Award the mark for stating that the rate increases as carbon dioxide concentration increases.

rubric.why: Explains why the rate does not keep increasing indefinitely.
rubric.description: The rate eventually levels off when another factor becomes limiting.
rubric.how: Award the mark for stating that the rate levels off or stops increasing because another factor is limiting.

modelAnswer: As carbon dioxide concentration increases, the rate of photosynthesis increases, provided other factors are not limiting.
The rate eventually levels off when another factor becomes limiting.

rubric.why: Identifies that aerobic respiration takes place when oxygen is present.
rubric.description: Aerobic respiration is respiration that takes place in the presence of oxygen.
rubric.how: Award the mark for stating that oxygen is present or required.

rubric.why: Describes the complete breakdown of glucose and the products and energy released.
rubric.description: Glucose is completely broken down to carbon dioxide and water, releasing energy.
rubric.how: Award the mark for identifying complete glucose breakdown, carbon dioxide and water as products, and energy release.

modelAnswer: Aerobic respiration is the process in which glucose is completely broken down in the presence of oxygen.
It releases energy and produces carbon dioxide and water.

items.followUp: What is appendicitis? Name one symptom.

rubric.why: Identifies the appendix and where it is attached.
rubric.description: The appendix is a small, blind-ended, finger-like tube attached to the caecum.
rubric.how: Award the mark for identifying it as a projection attached to the caecum.

rubric.why: Gives a valid symptom of appendicitis.
rubric.description: A symptom may be abdominal pain, often in the lower right part of the abdomen; nausea or fever may also occur.
rubric.how: Award the mark for any one valid symptom.

modelAnswer: The appendix is a small, blind-ended, finger-like tube attached to the caecum.
A symptom of appendicitis is abdominal pain, often in the lower right part of the abdomen; nausea or fever may also occur.

items.followUp: What distinguishes Rh-positive blood from Rh-negative blood?

rubric.why: Identifies the basis of the Rh blood group system.
rubric.description: The Rh system classifies blood according to whether the Rh (D) antigen is present on red blood cells.
rubric.how: Award the mark for stating that the system is based on the presence or absence of the Rh antigen on red blood cells.

rubric.why: Distinguishes Rh-positive blood from Rh-negative blood.
rubric.description: Rh-positive blood has the antigen, while Rh-negative blood lacks it.
rubric.how: Award the mark for correctly stating that Rh-positive blood has the antigen and Rh-negative blood lacks it.

modelAnswer: The Rh blood group system classifies blood according to whether the Rh (D) antigen is present on red blood cells.
Rh positive blood has this antigen, while Rh negative blood lacks it.
